analysis.title: Weekly Oil Data: Crude and product stocks build again
key_insights: US commercial crude stocks rose 3.4Mb w/w, versus consensus of a 58kb build and below the API-reported 5.3Mb increase reported the previous day.
SPR inventories fell 3.2Mb w/w, versus a 2.6Mb decline the previous week.
Refinery utilisation rose 50bps to 95.7%, versus a consensus increase of 20bps. US crude production edged up to 14.0Mb/d and net imports fell 2.2Mb/d.
Implied total product demand rose 0.6Mb/d w/w to 20.4Mb/d, led by distillate (+0.4Mb/d), with propane and fuel oil each up 0.2Mb/d. Jet fuel demand fell 0.2Mb/d.
The four-week average of implied product demand was flat w/w at 20.6Mb/d and 1% (about 0.2Mb/d) higher y/y.
Total product inventories rose 5.8Mb, supported by high refinery utilisation. Gasoline rose 5.2Mb (consensus +1.6Mb), jet fuel 2.2Mb and distillate 1.6Mb (consensus +1.3Mb).
Fuel ethanol stocks rose 0.6Mb, fuel oil and propane were broadly flat, and other oils fell 3.7Mb, partly offsetting the builds elsewhere.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Build much larger than the 58kb consensus, though smaller than the 5.3Mb API figure.
Consensus expected a near-flat week, so the actual build was a large bearish surprise for crude.
Industry data published the day before the EIA report, larger than the EIA figure.
SPR draws continued, faster than the previous week's 2.6Mb decline.
Higher than the 20bps consensus increase, which supports product builds.
Lower imports partly offset the supply increase from production and low draws.
Weekly demand improved, led by distillate.

macro_indicators.indicator: Implied total product demand, four-week average
macro_indicators.interpretation: Underlying demand is about 0.2Mb/d above last year.
Largest product build, well above the +1.6Mb consensus.
Consensus expected a much smaller build.
Consensus expected a slightly smaller build.
Jet fuel stocks built even as jet demand fell 0.2Mb/d.
A draw that partly offset builds elsewhere.

risk_factors: Oil prices are volatile in the short, medium and long term and are affected by unpredictable events, including natural disasters.
